additional_considerations.rationale: Usually hearing loss, tinnitus and episodic vertigo from endolymphatic disruption; may be unilateral or bilateral.
Antibiotic-related hearing loss is permanent; aspirin-related loss is reversible, so aspirin should be withheld during the workup.
Unlikely without other neurologic signs, but should be considered if focal deficits are found.

source_issues: Exam lines e003 ('HEENT:') and e013 ('Neuro:') are section headers with no findings; they are covered by listing them with the item lines that follow them.
Exam e018 'no past pointing and 8 heel to shin' contains an OCR artifact ('8'); the heel-to-shin result is not stated (x028).
The opening scenario omits the patient's sex; 'male' is taken from the raw patient description and the note.
Note HPI says cerumen removal gave 'moderate improvement'; the script says it gave only temporary relief and the hearing is now as bad as before.
p008 denies problems understanding speech, while p006 says words sound jumbled and distorted and p001 says he has been reading lips; the note also says 'no difficulty comprehending'.
annotator_notes: Header-only exam lines (e003, e004-e009 under HEENT; e013, e014-e018 under Neuro) are recorded by putting the header id together with the item id in exam_ids.

All three hearing-related sp_notes directions (bilateral hearing difficulty, no Weber lateralization, cannot hear when spoken to from behind) are recorded as sp_notes exam findings (x015-x017) and also kept as acting notes.
p007 'Yes' (can identify the source of sound) is recorded as an absent difficulty localizing sound (f008).
p013 (falls / sensation of impending falls) is split into two absent facts.
